Incident Report #2000 covers operational behavior observed on payments-api in eu-central-1 between 08:00 and 11:30 UTC. Monitoring alerts triggered when p95 request latency crossed 435 ms and HTTP 5xx error rates reached 13.25 percent across worker nodes. At peak load, resident memory climbed to 2110 MB while background compaction jobs competed with interactive API traffic for CPU time.

Subsystem trace 1 (redis-eviction) recorded Redis volatile-lru memory eviction and latency spikes during a burst of 180 requests per second lasting 23 minutes. Engineers inspected kernel page cache pressure, connection pool wait queues, and lock contention metrics across primary and replica hosts. Temporary rate limits reduced tail latency by 29 percent, but batch workers still queued behind synchronous database writes whenever checkpoint intervals overlapped with scheduled reporting jobs. Mitigation steps included raising pool timeouts, isolating long-running exports to a separate worker queue, lowering per-request memory caps, adding explicit circuit breakers on slow upstream calls, and scheduling automated regression checks before re-enabling full concurrency.
